findings.name: stock-db
findings.root_cause: stock-db is OOMKilled (exit 137) because its memory limit/request of 24Mi is far too small for loading the stock index into memory; each crash takes port 5432 down, so stock-api sees 'stock-db:5432 unreachable', exhausts its 3 retries and exits with FATAL, entering a restart loop.
findings.fix: Raise the stock-db container memory request/limit well above 24Mi (e.g. 256Mi or more based on the stock-index size) so it survives the index load; optionally make stock-api tolerate transient DB outages instead of exiting after 3 attempts.

diagnosis.summary: stock-api's crash loop is a symptom, not the cause. Its logs show repeated 'stock-db:5432 unreachable' followed by 'FATAL: database unavailable after 3 attempts, exiting'. The real failure is stock-db: its container is OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts) because the Deployment sets a 24Mi memory limit while the workload loads a stock index into memory; every kill drops port 5432, which starves stock-api until it gives up and exits. Fix: raise stock-db's memory limit in the stock-db Deployment."

findings.name: billing
findings.root_cause: The billing container declares envFrom configMap "billing-config", but no ConfigMap named billing-config exists in the billing namespace, so kubelet cannot create the container (CreateContainerConfigError) and the pod stays Pending, never reaching Running.
findings.fix: Create the missing ConfigMap billing-config in namespace billing with the keys the app expects (or remove the envFrom reference from the Deployment if it is not needed).

diagnosis.summary: billing/billing-597d6775c9-ht8g5 is stuck in Pending with CreateContainerConfigError: the container's envFrom references ConfigMap \"billing-config\", which does not exist in the billing namespace (only kube-root-ca.crt is present). The Deployment has 0/1 ready replicas. Fix: create the billing-config ConfigMap (or drop the envFrom reference).

findings.name: orders-api
findings.root_cause: orders-api pod crashes on startup with 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set' (exit 1) because the Deployment defines no env or envFrom at all, so the required database connection string is never provided; the container crash-loops and the deployment has 0 ready replicas, taking the orders page down.
findings.fix: Add the missing configuration to the orders-api Deployment: set the DATABASE_URL environment variable (or mount an envFrom ConfigMap/Secret containing it) so the app can start, then let the pod restart cleanly.

diagnosis.summary: orders/orders-api is crash-looping: the container exits 1 immediately with 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set'. The Deployment spec has no env/envFrom entries, so the required database URL is never injected. No other workloads in the namespace are affected; there are no Services here. Fix: supply DATABASE_URL via env or an envFrom ConfigMap/Secret on the orders-api Deployment."

findings.fix: Remove the custom dnsConfig from the mailer Deployment (or set dnsPolicy to ClusterFirst) so pods use cluster DNS instead of non-resolving nameserver 10.96.0.99.
findings.name: mailer
findings.root_cause: mailer crash-loops with 'nc: bad address smtp-relay' because its pod has dnsPolicy None and a custom nameserver 10.96.0.99 that does not resolve in-cluster service names; the relay is healthy (service has 1 ready endpoint), so this is a DNS misconfiguration on mailer, not a downed relay.

diagnosis.summary: mailer cannot reach smtp-relay, but the relay is not down: Service smtp-relay has 1 matching pod and 1 ready endpoint on port 25. The mailer pod's logs show 'nc: bad address smtp-relay', i.e. a DNS resolution failure, and the pod spec has dnsPolicy None with a custom nameserver 10.96.0.99 that evidently does not answer for in-cluster service names. Root cause is the mailer Deployment's DNS configuration; fixing it (ClusterFirst / remove custom dnsConfig) restores name resolution.

diagnosis.summary: statement-builder in finance crash-loops with OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts). The team set no memory limit, but the namespace LimitRange 'defaults' applies a 32Mi default memory limit / 16Mi request to containers without one; the container spec shows limits.memory=32Mi and its workload exceeds it, causing repeated kills. Fix: raise the LimitRange default or give the Deployment an explicit larger memory limit.

findings.name: report-worker
findings.root_cause: report-worker container is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137) because its memory limit of 32Mi is too low for the workload; the kernel kills the process before any application error can be logged, so logs show only 'warming report cache' and the pod restarts every few seconds.
findings.fix: Raise the report-worker container memory limit (and request) above its actual working set, e.g. from 32Mi/16Mi to at least 128Mi, then verify the process stays alive.

diagnosis.summary: report-worker in namespace reports crash-loops with exit code 137 / reason OOMKilled (3 restarts). The container's memory limit is 32Mi (request 16Mi), which the workload exceeds within seconds of starting, so the kernel kills it before any application error appears in the logs — matching the user's observation of restarts with no error. Fix: raise the memory limit on the Deployment.

findings.name: search-web
findings.root_cause: The liveness probe runs a busy-loop (300k shell iterations) before its wget, with timeoutSeconds=1 and a 10m CPU limit; the probe times out, kubelet kills the healthy nginx (SIGQUIT, exit 0), so logs show no app errors but the pod crash-loops.
findings.fix: Remove the busy-loop from the liveness exec probe (use plain `wget -q -O /dev/null http://127.0.0.1/` or an HTTP GET probe) and raise the CPU limit above 10m so the probe has time to complete.

diagnosis.summary: search-web restarts every few minutes with no app errors because its liveness probe is broken: it runs a 300,000-iteration shell busy-loop before the health-check wget, with only a 1s timeout on a container capped at 10m CPU. The probe always times out (events show 'command timed out'), kubelet sends SIGQUIT to the perfectly healthy nginx (logs show clean shutdown, exit code 0), and the pod enters CrashLoopBackOff. Fix is in the Deployment's livenessProbe spec (and the too-low CPU limit).

findings.root_cause: session-svc proxies /login to auth-api over HTTPS and fails verification with 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)', returning 502; the auth-api leaf cert (CN=auth-api, issuer Internal Services CA 2026) lapsed 2026-09-26.
findings.fix: Renew the auth-api leaf certificate from Internal Services CA 2026 (lapsed 2026-09-26), update the auth-api-tls secret served on port 443, and republish it in the auth-api-cert ConfigMap. No client trust change needed.

rejected_submission.summary: Logins fail with 502 through session-svc because upstream auth-api presents an expired TLS cert. session-svc nginx logs show repeated 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)' against https://10.96.14.154:443/login (auth-api Service), each followed by a 502. The public cert in auth-api-cert/tls.crt (CN=auth-api, issuer Internal Services CA 2026) shows not_after 2026-09-26T13:07:05Z — expired one day before the report. The CA is valid for 10 years, so this is a leaf expiry, not a trust mismatch. Both pods are running/ready; nothing was deployed today — the cert simply lapsed. Fix: renew the auth-api leaf cert from the same CA, update the auth-api-tls secret, and republish auth-api-cert.
